sections.h2: Is a quick sale the right move for a Kennesaw house?
sections.html:
A quick sale fits Kennesaw owners who face repairs, an estate to settle or a payment problem, while a full listing suits those with time and a tidy house. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate for the city is 37,970 residents, against 33,036 counted in 2020. That growth keeps buyers active, though it also puts many listings near the university and along Cobb Parkway.

Speed matters most when a house needs work, sits empty or carries a loan you cannot keep paying. In those cases weigh the closing date and repair bill against the price. Write down the net under each route before choosing one.

sections.h2: Where is Kennesaw and what are its homes like?
sections.html:
Kennesaw covers about 9.5 square miles in northwest Cobb County, with Acworth on its northwest edge and Kennesaw Mountain just southeast of the limits inside the battlefield park. The summit stands 1,808 feet above sea level, the highest spot in the Atlanta area, and the city took its name from it. Until 1887 the settlement was called Big Shanty, after the shanties built for railroad crews.

U.S. 41 and State Route 3 run through town as Cobb Parkway, and Interstate 75 clips the northeast corner with exits 269, 271 and 273. Downtown Atlanta is about 27 miles southeast. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau counts 13,554 households, 64.6 percent of them owner occupied, with a median home value of $335,400 and median gross rent of $1,845. Renting is an option if you inherit and prefer not to sell right away.

  • Median household income: $83,356 (in 2024 dollars)
  • Mean commute: 28.6 minutes
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 47.3 percent

sections.h2: What drives buyer demand around Kennesaw?
sections.html:
Kennesaw State University is the biggest anchor, described as the third-largest public university in Georgia, so ask a local agent how much nearby demand ties back to the campus. The Southern Museum of Civil War and Locomotive History downtown recalls the Great Locomotive Chase of April 12, 1862, and the battlefield park draws visitors all year. The Big Shanty Festival each April reportedly brings more than 60,000 people downtown.

Census retail sales for 2022 came to about $1.76 billion, a figure that points to a regional shopping and commuting center. Houses a short drive from the I-75 exits are the easiest for a buyer to place on a map.

The battlefield park holds about 18 miles of trails and historic Civil War sites, and the city earned a Preserve America Community designation in March 2004. A 1861 to 1863 training camp, Camp MacDonald, once stood in the area, and the Kennesaw Cemetery holds graves dating to the 1860s. Mentioning the trails and downtown depot in a listing gives walkable-history buyers a reason to look.

sections.h2: What do Cobb's wet summers do to a Kennesaw house?
sections.html:
They wear on roofs, gutters, crawl spaces and exterior paint. Kennesaw's humid subtropical climate averages roughly 54.6 inches of rain a year, and summer highs have reached 104 degrees. An inspector hired by a buyer will start with drainage, moisture and the age of the HVAC system.

Selling as is, expect those items to set the price. Listing instead, a modest round of fixes to flashing, grading and mechanicals often costs less than the discount requested after inspection.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Kennesaw house, and when is it due?
sections.html:
Kennesaw owners get two tax bills. Cobb County collects for itself and the school district, and the city runs a separate city bill. The county values property at 40 percent of market value, and its 2026 bills went out in August with an October 15, 2026 payment date. City bills are mailed October 1 and carry a December 1 due date.

The city says its tax covers the full year with no proration, so sharing the bill with a buyer is a contract term. Before signing, ask your closing attorney how each of the two bills will show on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Kennesaw city taxes?
sections.html:
Interest begins the morning after the due date. The city then layers on a 5 percent penalty at 120 days and a further 5 percent every 120 days after that, stopping at 20 percent of principal. It also runs an annual tax sale on the first Tuesday in November at City Hall, starting at 9:00 AM, advertised in the Marietta Daily Journal four weeks beforehand.

Pay off any open city or county balance before you take an offer. Title work will find it, and the payoff would otherwise be taken from what you receive.

sections.h2: Can a Kennesaw house that ran as an Airbnb be sold?
sections.html:
It can be sold, though the rental permission may stay behind. The city's short-term rental ordinance (Chapter 22, Article XIII) covers any dwelling let for fewer than 30 consecutive days and calls for both a city business license and a Short-Term Rental Certificate, which expires every December 31. The application fee is $250.

A house operating before January 1, 2025 could register as nonconforming, but the city states that status ends automatically when ownership changes. A new owner who wants nightly guests must meet the current rules: the 8 percent hotel and motel excise tax, the two-property maximum and the 250-foot distance requirement that nonconforming rentals skip. Explain this to buyers early. The Business License Office is at 3080 Moon Station Road.

sections.h2: What permit and records issues come up in Kennesaw sales?
sections.html:
Open permits cause the most trouble, so ask the city's building and inspections staff whether any permit on the house was left unclosed. Unfinished work from a past owner can stall a buyer with a loan even when a cash buyer would take it as is. Cobb County Fire covers the city, while Kennesaw keeps its own police department and 9-1-1 center at City Hall.

  • Collect permit records and receipts for roof, HVAC and electrical jobs.
  • Confirm no city or county tax balance is outstanding.
  • For a former rental, ask the Business License Office which registrations are still active.

On the state side, Georgia's transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100, and the Department of Revenue says it is paid before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: How soon could a cash sale close in Kennesaw?
faqs.a: Timing rests on the title search and the buyer, but a cash deal skips underwriting and the lender's appraisal, usually the slowest steps. Leave room for title work and for the transfer tax filing with the Clerk of Superior Court.

faqs.q: Do Cobb and Kennesaw send separate tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes. Cobb bills county and school taxes, and the city mails its own bill October 1 with a December 1 due date. Because the city does not prorate, the split with a buyer is set in your contract.

faqs.q: Is it worth appealing a Cobb assessment before a sale?
faqs.a: Only if the value looks high and the window is open. Owners get 45 days from the date printed on the Notice of Assessment, and the 2026 notices were mailed June 5.

faqs.q: Will my homestead exemption follow the house to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The exemption depends on you owning and living in the home on January 1, and Cobb's assessor listed July 20 as the 2026 filing deadline. Kennesaw also offers its own city exemption for owners 65 and older, applied for by April 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kennesaw house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes, as is. Expect the offer to reflect the repair cost, and keep permit records on hand so the buyer's inspection and title review go smoothly.
